name: pdk-bitstring-etl
instr:
Our controller team now generates telemetry record layouts from their C headers as struct format strings. Our decoder hands each layout to bitstring, since the records also carry bit fields between the structs, like `<IHH?x, u3, bool, u4, <8s?`. bitstring only knows the numeric struct codes, so most layouts fail. Monday's captures, the layouts and our scripts are in /data/telemetry.

A struct group is `<`, `>` or `!` followed by any codes struct accepts after them, with counts as struct uses them. Wherever a group sits in a format (a string or a list, with repeats, brackets and keyword lengths) and at whatever bit position, `Bits.unpack`, `Reader.read_list` and `pack` should give exactly what `struct.unpack` and `struct.pack` give for it. A single code holding one value, such as `<?` or `!12p`, should read and write the same way anywhere a dtype is accepted, `Array` included, as `>h` already does.

Out of range integers, a str or int for `s` or `p`, and `c` bytes that aren't one byte long should raise `ValueError`. A record that runs past the end of the data raises `ReadError` and leaves the Reader where it was. `@`, `=` and codes with only a native size still raise `ValueError`.

/data/telemetry/replay_setpoints.py packs Monday's setpoints, and every record it packs should match the controllers' echo and trend files byte for byte.

Keep the existing tests in /app/tests passing and follow /app/AGENTS.md for docs and release notes. There's no network; everything is installed i
